page0.text:
And then, I wake up.
I don't feel tired. My mind and body are refreshed, like they belong to someone else.

page1.text:
"...Huh, Senpai?"
He was supposed to be sleeping next to me, but nobody else is in my futon.
I look at the clock and see that it's already ten o'clock in the morning.
"Oh, he went to make breakfast."
I pretend to accept that and get up.

page2.text:
I'm surprised by my lightness.
What's going on, I wonder.
It's as if my arms and legs have been freed from a lifetime of chains.

page3.text:
"Ah... Um, right."
I remember, and my body heats up.
Last night, Senpai shared his blood with me, and we slept together.
...When we came back from the forest, Senpai only had one arm, but we were sure things would work out.
I'm feeling fine, so I can ask Rider to help out.

page4.text:
Nothing bad will happen aymore.
I have Senpai and Nee-san. We'll all do great, and...

page5.text:
"Ah...ngh."
...A nightmare.
Why do I dream about the worst events?

page6.text:
"Senpai?"
The breeze coming in feels nice.
The corridor is bathed in light, and walking through it lifts my spirits.
My body feels so light.
Maybe I even lost weight while I was asleep.

page7.text:
...To be honest, I'm a little on the heavy side, and I do battle with the bathroom scale every night.
It hasn't really been working, but if Senpai says something like,
"Sakura, you look slender in everything, huh?"
It'll make me swoon, so I'm certainly in favor of this newfound weight loss.

page8.text:
"Senpai...?"
My body really feels so light and relaxed, it feels like the world is changing with each step I take.

page9.text:
My body is so light.
The air is so beautiful.
The pulsing is so warm.

page10.text:
It's like I've been freed from a poison permeating my body.
Like the worms Grandfather implanted in me,
like the black mud sticking to my heart,
like the awful dreams lingering in the back of my mind never happened at all...

page11.text:
"Hey, Senpai?"
Nobody's here.
The hallway is very quiet.

page12.text:
"Senpai... Senpai...?"
Nobody's here.
The sunshine is warm.

page13.text:
"Senpai... Sen...pai...? Oh, are we playing hide and seek?"
Nobody's here.
The air is crisp.

page14.text:
"Huh... That's...weird. Wha... Senpai is just hiding...but..."
That can't be right.
Somebody has to be here.
It was just a bad dream,

page15.text:
but I saw someone at the end.
His body was totally broken, and they would never meet again—

page16.text:
"No... It, it isn't true, right, Senpai?"
Of course it isn't true.
His body wasn't human anymore.
He couldn't possibly move in that body, so he should be staying here, waiting somewhere for me to come—

page17.text:
"Senpai... Sen...pai."
But...
The calendar in the living room shows that it's already been over ten days. It's the end of February.

page18.text:
"Ah... No..."
I collapse to my knees.
I understand everything now.
No, I knew as soon I woke up, but I pretended not to.

page19.text:
"No... Come out, please come out, Senpai...!
I... I can't... I can't do this by myself, Senpai. I can't go on without you, Senpai. Senpai, Senpai, Senpaiii...!!!"

page20.text:
My personality goes blank.
Even now, I'm about to collapse but can't collapse. I can only weep.
That's really all it is.
I'm a weakling, a crybaby, I don't know any other way to atone, and I can't even be grateful for being alive.

page21.text:
It's the end of a long winter.
I've been freed from the chains binding me for the last eleven years, but I lost my only guidepost.

page22.text:
"...Haah. You're so stubborn, Sakura. I underestimated you."
The boy speaks sullenly.
He sighs with a frustrated expression.
...She was prepared for that.
She made contact with him, assuming that he would dislike her and that she would cause him trouble.

page23.text:
It was but a slight touch.
A part of her thought it would hurt if the boy disliked her, while...
"Oh, start over from this part. I'm going to be counting on you, so you can't ask me for help.
—Thanks, Sakura. I'll have you help me until my injury gets better.
She saw how the boy muttered it to hide his embarrassment, and she cherished his generosity of spirit.

page25.text:
"...Whew. That settles one thing, Sakura.
The Association's investigation is over, and Kirei's replacement seems decent. They're not going to punish us.
This is a happy ending, right?"

page26.text:
Nee-san is strong.
She wasn't any more energetic than I was, but her spirits lifted when spring came, and she's working her brain.

page27.text: "By the way, Sakura, want to come live at my house? If you're moving out of the Matou house, it'd be easier for you to come over, right?"

page28.text:
Nee-san's consideration is so kind.
I've dreamed for years about living in the Tohsaka house with my sister.
I can't stand being alone at night, and even today, I'm not sure what will happen if she comes home.
But...
That's why I need to grow up.

page29.text: "...I see. You're going to strike out on your own. Then I won't pressure you. I'll be around until I graduate, so feel free to come hang out on your days off."

page30.text:
She tells me she'll be waiting, and leaves.
...It must have been stuck in her hair when she came here.
A pink flower petal flutters through the air.

page31.text:
"Hm? Is this your first time cooking, Sakura?"
It wasn't, but I can't say I was familiar with it yet.
I did my best to read a lot of books before I came, and I was about average in cooking class.
To tell the truth, though, I was very, very afraid to have anyone eat something I cooked.

page32.text:
"...No. I can make simple things."
"That's not what I meant, um... well, you'll just learn as you go.
Okay, I'll start from the basics. Here. Careful, it's hot."

page33.text:
The basic dish was rice balls.
We took steaming hot rice and squeezed it together.
I thought he was making fun of me.
I sulked a little, thinking that it was beneath me.
But when I looked up, I saw that his face was deadly serious, and I couldn't feel upset.
And then...

page34.text:
"Okay, let's trade. I'll give you my rice ball, and I'll eat yours."
He took the rice ball I just made and stuffed his cheeks with it, right in front of me.
He gobbled up something I made and put his hands together in thanks.

page35.text:
I don't know what he was trying to tell me.
But the next day, I didn't feel as self-conscious about my cooking, and I wanted him to eat it and thank me again.

page37.text: "...Are you sure, Sakura? It would help us out a lot if you took over, but..."

page38.text:
I earned a surprising amount of money from selling the Matou house.
It's more than enough to maintain this one.
I asked Ms. Fujimura's grandfather to give me the deed to the property, and decided to keep this place the way it is, no matter what happens from now on.

page39.text:
"...I'm happy you care so much.
Look, Sakura. Shirou isn't coming—"

page40.text:
I shake my head.
Ms. Fujimura's shoulders droop in resignation.
"All right. I'll leave this house to you."
She smiled like a mother, and left the Emiya house.

page41.text: This...is kind of a tough memory for me.

page42.text:
"...Sakura. Once this commotion is over, let's go someplace far away.
You've never taken a vacation anywhere, have you? It could be fun to go on a trip."

page43.text:
He said that there was nowhere we couldn't go if we put our minds to it.
It was so pure that I laughed.

page44.text: "...Okay, it's a promise. Once you get better and this is all over..."

page46.text:
Spring comes.
I think I haven't met anyone for a while.

page47.text:
It's difficult being alone.
I keep repeating my memories. I want to turn them off like a light switch.
It helps that I don't long for company, but then why did I...

page48.text: —...Of course I am. You need to take responsibility for what you've done, Sakura.—

page49.text:
...Ahh, I need to do something.
It's hard being alone and with other people, but I... I need to do what I can...

page50.text:
But I don't know how to atone.
After all this time, I can't think of a way to help anyone else.
Because this is for myself.
I've been growing one flower every year, for that promised day.

page52.text:
I'm used to being alone. I can enjoy myself a little when people are around.
But the fear is still there.
I talk to people, but I feel like the world is demanding that I atone.

page53.text: —But I'll protect you. I'll protect you from everything people will ask you. Even if it's hypocritical, I've always tried to live up to the ideal of protecting the people I love.—

page54.text:
He was so selfish.
It was so nasty of him to say all that and then not protect me.
So I can't forgive him so easily.
I'm going to be really selfish and make him go through the trouble I had to many times over.

page55.text:
Mm... But I think I'll forgive him anyway.
It might be hypocritical, but his words calm my heart so much.
It might be irresponsible, but I love the boy who said that to me, and he loves me, too.

page61.text:
I'm not sad about it.
But sometimes, I feel so calm waiting for spring to come that I wonder if I'm still sane.

page62.text:
I'm not sad because something is absolute.
Because I believe that something will happen that makes up for the suffering.
I only have one worry.

page63.text: "...Senpai sure is taking a while. I'm going to be an old woman, at this rate."

page64.text: I pray that I can stay healthy until that day comes.

page65.text:
Spring comes.
Lately, I haven't been able to move my body as well as I'd like.
I go out to water the garden as usual.

page66.text:
"Sensei! I'm here to help!"
My student is here.
I'm self-taught and not very skilled, but I found a student willing to learn from me.
The new Tohsaka heir is a good girl. She's very similar to my sister.

page67.text:
Light scatters.
I sit in my rocking chair in its usual place, and gaze out at the yard.

page68.text: "Oh, Sensei. Please don't sleep, okay? I want to hear more stories when I finish."

page69.text:
That brings me great joy.
All I can remember are words now, but words only need to be spoken in order to become stories. They let me relive nostalgic days.

page70.text: "Ah, you smiled. I love it when you smile. You're so beautiful, unlike my greedy grandma."

page71.text:
The sunlight is warm. Time flows gently, and sometimes, torturously.
I keep planting seeds in anticipation of that promised day.
Flowers of redemption.
I'll keep waiting for spring until my sins are forgiven.

page73.text:
The years pass by in the blink of an eye.
I close and open my eyes.
The hill is covered in cherry blossoms.
Looking just as he always has, the boy waves at me from the hilltop road of our youth.
